title: MR1 · Recover degraded land
description: Seed-grown carob in favourable rootable and moisture pockets; irregular mixed groups and retained open ground.
limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

title: MR2 · Rainfall capture
description: Conceptual planting islands, donor catchment and safe overflow. MR1 and MR2 can be combined.
limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

title: Assumed moisture pocket
description: A configurable assumed pocket introduces one encina example. Its size does not establish water availability or oak suitability.
limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

title: Stone surface mulch
description: Surface stone cover around selected plants; not a buried drainage layer. Ring dimensions are project assumptions.
limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

title: Density and area basis
description: Pies/ha means individual trees or stems per hectare. MR1 passages give <350, <100 and <200 in different contexts: no single target is inferred. Whole-zone density differs from spacing within groups; carob, total trees and shrubs are separate.
limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

title: Planting season and stock
description: For limited-care restoration plant in autumn and avoid delays, especially on shallow or stony soils. Una savia means one growing season (1+0); >200 cm³ is >0.2 L. Table 5.14 gives November–March and 200–300 cm³; these contexts differ. Larger stock is not automatically better.
limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

title: Reported Almería survival
description: The handbook reports 40–60% carob survival in Almería (Planelles et al., 2001), without a monitoring period here. Historical evidence, not an annual probability or a forecast for this zone.
limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

title: Low-maintenance protective restoration
description: Routine field fertilizer, formation pruning and continuing competition control are generally omitted. Table 5.14 also lists establishment weeding. This is a protective-management baseline, not proof of maximum growth or zero establishment water.
limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

title: Illustrative geometry and quantities
description: Deterministic layout, starter counts, footprints, pocket and mulch dimensions are editable project assumptions. Circles are planning footprints, not root zones or measured mature crowns.
limitations: No source supplies these exact generated coordinates or universally optimal quantities.

title: Oak and companion context
description: Coscoja is usually a shrub; its natural occurrence near 200 mm annual rainfall at Cabo de Gata is not a seedling survival guarantee. Encina is a conditional larger-tree candidate for favourable soil/moisture pockets. Cork oak needs suitable soil chemistry and moisture; myrtle is a moisture-pocket candidate. Phillyrea angustifolia and P. latifolia are distinct taxa. A vegetation series describes reference communities and related stages, not a mandatory planting mix or a guarantee of tall forest.
limitations: No series or species suitability is assigned to this assumed zone. Rainfall alone is insufficient.
